title: Structured-output roundtrip and toolcall idempotency regression suite
creator: Leah Kim
description: Create a deterministic regression suite that validates structured-output fidelity end-to-end and asserts idempotent semantics for tool/function calls across streaming, chunked-output, and retry/fallback scenarios. This ticket defines the tests, implements harnesses, and wires the jobs into CI so we catch breaking changes to API contracts that affect downstream SDKs and integrations.
goal: Prevent regressions where structured JSON/NDJSON outputs drift or tool calls are repeated/duplicated when requests traverse retry/fallback paths or when streaming boundaries change. Provide clear CI signal and actionable diffs for engineers on failure.
scope: Golden prompt corpus for structured-output roundtrips (schemas and typing), toolcall idempotency scenarios (single-shot, streaming multi-chunk, retry-after-fallback), and a small set of backward-compat smoke cases for clients that rely on streaming ordering and partial-output semantics. Excludes large-scale load testing and external partner contracts (tracked separately).
steps: Design canonical schema set (4 schemas) and example prompt+expected canonical outputs (golden corpus)
Implement roundtrip validator that re-parses generated structured output, normalizes timestamps/ids, and diffs against golden canonical outputs using token-insensitive matching rules
Build toolcall idempotency harness that simulates: a) duplicate tool-call delivery, b) truncated streaming chunks, c) replays from prefix caches
Add backpressure and chunk boundary fuzzing layer to ensure partial-object streaming does not yield invalid JSON or duplicate tool invocations
Create CI jobs: conformance/structured-roundtrip and conformance/toolcall-idempotency with clear junit-style artifacts and golden-diff snapshots
Wire failing runs to PR blocking gates for runtime and SDK repos and publish triage playbook for engineers
acceptance_criteria: Two green CI jobs in main with deterministic outputs on baseline commit (conformance/structured-roundtrip, conformance/toolcall-idempotency)
Golden corpus stored under repo path and accessible to test runners; failure artifacts include normalized diffs and example request/response traces
Harness simulates streaming boundary shifts and proves function-call deduplication behavior for 3 representative models/quantizations
Runbook created describing triage steps and who to page for model, runtime, or SDK regressions
At least one flaky historical failure reproduced and prevented by the new suite (documented)
progress_updates: 2026-02-17 - Leah Kim: Drafted golden schemas and initial prompt corpus (4 scenarios). Added canonical normalization rules for timestamps and client-generated ids.

2026-02-22 - Ravi Patel: Prototype roundtrip validator implemented; found a mismatch in streaming chunk reassembly for model-variant v1.19-quant. Created minimal failing test to demonstrate the issue.
2026-03-01 - Design review (Anya Park): Confirmed schemas cover nested arrays and toolcall metadata; suggested adding a case for binary-blob references in structured output.

2026-03-05 - Ravi Patel: Implemented toolcall idempotency harness to simulate duplicate event delivery and retry-after-timeout. Observed duplicated tool invocation when helper middleware did not attach idempotency-key.
2026-03-09 - PR opened (see code_links) to add two CI jobs and upload initial golden corpus. Seeking review from runtime and SDK leads.
decisions: Use token-insensitive diffing (structural JSON diff after normalization) to avoid noise from whitespace/ordering and non-deterministic fields
Normalize ephemeral fields (timestamps, request-ids) instead of stubbing in tests to enable compatibility across environments
Keep golden corpus compact (4 robust scenarios) to keep CI cheap; larger corpora will live in nightly regression bucket
Simulate idempotency at harness layer with explicit idempotency-key header; do not change runtime behavior in tests unless reproducing a real bug
ci_config: conformance/structured-roundtrip (fast, matrix across model-variants: v1.19, v1.20-quant) and conformance/toolcall-idempotency (simulation mode). Jobs run on PRs touching runtime or SDK surface areas and nightly on main.
notes: Reviewer feedback (2026-03-02, Miguel Lopez): Add a small heuristic to detect semantic JSON drift where field types flip (number -> string).
Follow-up: schedule a cross-team sync with SDK and QA to agree on failure signal semantics and triage owners (runtime vs sdk).
Potential extension: add a lightweight property-based test that generates chunk boundaries to stress streaming parser (planned for Cycle 2026-W14).
